summary: The raw-pair argument is mathematically sound. Positive raw-pair volume yields a full-dimensional symmetric pair body whose centroid has integral base coordinate; Prékopa and Grünbaum give at least V/e mass on the relevant continuous-coordinate side, the accepted symmetric lattice sampling inequality costs 2^n, and endpoint pairing costs 2, producing the claimed V/(e 2^(n+1)) bound for every proper halfspace. The whole-space, zero-volume, shear-invariance, supremum, product-core, and triangular calibration cases are all handled correctly, including boundary and lower-dimensional sections.
